learning_objective: 🧪 Discover the incredible chemicals of life—proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids—and learn how enzymes speed up biological reactions!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Primary metabolites (amino acids, sugars) have identifiable functions and are essential for normal physiological processes. Secondary metabolites (rubber, essential oils, antibiotics, spices) are mostly produced by plants/fungi for defense or ecology.

Proteins are long chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. They have 4 levels of structure: Primary (sequence), Secondary (helices/sheets), Tertiary (3D folding, essential for enzymes), and Quaternary (multiple folded chains like Hemoglobin).

Polysaccharides are chains of sugars (like starch for storage in plants, glycogen in animals, cellulose for structure). Lipids are not strictly macromolecules (they are small but clump together); they include fats, oils, and phospholipids (cell membranes).
Made of nucleotides (a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base). DNA is a double helix held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases (A pairs with T, G pairs with C).

Almost all enzymes are proteins. They work by lowering the 'Activation Energy' needed to start a reaction. They act like a lock, and the substrate is the key. Factors like temperature and pH heavily affect their shape and function.

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Enzyme Lock and Key
fun_activity.instructions: Think of an enzyme as a highly specific padlock and the substrate as a key. If you heat the padlock too much (high temperature) or throw acid on it (extreme pH), the metal warps (denaturation). The key will no longer fit, and the reaction stops!

exam_tips: 📌 RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere, and Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world.
📌 Know the Zwitterionic form of an amino acid: it's a structure where both positive (NH3+) and negative (COO-) charges exist on the same molecule depending on the pH.
📌 Competitive inhibition is a frequent exam topic: A chemical structurally similar to the substrate competes for the enzyme's active site (e.g., malonate inhibiting succinic dehydrogenase).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Watson-Crick model describes DNA as a right-handed double helix with anti-parallel strands.
⭐ Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose and is the most abundant organic chemical on Earth.
⭐ Co-factors (like metal ions or coenzymes) are non-protein parts attached to an enzyme to make it catalytically active.
